summary: Foundations for auto-resume after a usage limit, for every chat, behind the staged flag limit_auto_resume (LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME_ENABLED in src/shared/limit-resume.ts, false; SB_LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME=1 or the backend setting labs.limit_auto_resume turns it on). This change adds the limit_resumes table (one row per root conversation: instance, limited turn, reset time, state, request id, streak, disarm reason), its CRUD, the setting chats.autoResumeAfterLimit (on by default), and the pure rules limitState, shouldArm, fireChecks, nextStreak and the resume turn wrapper, with shared fixtures. With the flag off (the default), no behaviour changes. The migration time is logged through the db.migrate perf span. Limit classification: the Claude and Codex adapters put an optional limit { limitClass, resetAt } on the end event of a turn that ended on a usage limit or a full context window (no limit means other), the registry logs one 'turn limit' counter line per such turn, and the synthetic model name the Claude CLI writes on its limit messages is never recorded or shown as the model. Only the flag-gated runner below reads the limit field. Desktop runner (this change, still behind the flag): src/main/provider/limit-resume.ts arms the chat's row on the end event of a usage-limited turn with a reset time, keeps one timer per armed row at the reset plus a minute (rebuilt at startup), and at fire time checks again (still armed with the same request id, not archived, no open card, same account, a fresh usage reading says the window is open). It then sends the wrapped resume turn through the approval result turn path and releases the held queue behind it, stores a [[sb:limit-resume]] row and publishes limit-resume.changed. A resumed turn that fails or hits the limit again within 5 minutes counts in the streak; the third gives up. Stop (interrupt), archive, Cancel auto-resume and a normal turn end before the reset disarm the row durably. Channels provider:limit-resume-enabled, -get, -cancel and -resume-now; the desktop Limited row (LimitResumeRow: Resumes HH:MM, Resume now, Cancel auto-resume) and the Settings, Accounts switch Resume after a usage limit resets show only while the flag is on. Every fire logs a limit-resume.fire perf span with its outcome, and arms, give-ups and resumed-turn outcomes log one info line each, so resume success can be counted. Phones and push (this change, still behind the flag): the backend advertises capability limit_auto_resume_v1 (the provider:limit-resume-* channels and limit-resume.changed exist; with the flag off, get answers none, so no row shows). The Expo thread screen shows the same Limited row as the desktop (LimitResumeRow: Resumes HH:MM, Resume now, Cancel auto-resume, or why no resume is armed), read on open and on every limit-resume.changed; an older backend without the capability keeps the held message's Resume only. limit-resume.changed carries gaveUp on the one change that gave up, and the push notifier sends 'Auto-resume gave up after 3 tries. Resume by hand.' for it. The give-up count is the existing 'limit resume outcome' line with gaveUp true; the Limited row reads go through the generic slow IPC span. Polish (still behind the flag): the desktop Limited row is a card with a clock icon, the state as its title and limitStateDetail (src/shared/limit-resume.ts, the line the phone Limited rows are to show under the same title) as its detail line, a Resume now refusal on its own alert line, Resume now filled and Cancel auto-resume outlined. The Settings switch moved into a Usage limits section after Add agent, as a SettingRow with the shared Switch (ui/switch.tsx, now also behind ToggleControl and the worktree protection switches); its row SETTING_ROW.autoResumeAfterLimit joins search and the changed counts once LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME_ENABLED is true. Phone Limited rows (still behind the flag): the Expo row now shows limitStateDetail under its title, with Resume now filled and Cancel auto-resume outlined, as the desktop row does. The native Android thread screen shows the same row (LimitResume.kt ports LimitState, limitStateText and limitStateDetail; ThreadSessionCoordinator reads provider:limit-resume-get on open, on any limit-resume.changed and after a replay gap, and sends Resume now and Cancel auto-resume) only against a backend with limit_auto_resume_v1; an older backend keeps the held message's Resume only. tests/fixtures/limit-resume-cases.json gains a limitStateText section (title and detail for every state) that vitest and the Kotlin port both run. The phone rows add no new backend cost: their reads go through the generic slow IPC span. End to end test (tests/unit/limit-resume-e2e.test.ts): the real registry, runner and limit_resumes table with a fake adapter and a fake clock, fed the Claude and Codex limit fixtures through the real adapters, cover arm, fire after the reset, one resume turn, the held queue in order, Stop, archive and Cancel, the give-up after three quick limits and the timer rebuilt after a restart. It found one bug, fixed here: the resume turn was not counted as an outstanding turn while held messages were, so the last queued message ran with no turn counted. Review of that test found two more, fixed with their own tests: a turn sent while the fire read usage still got the resume turn sent beside it (busy is now read again after the reading), and the Claude adapter ended a rejected turn twice (the rejection, then its late empty result), so the registry lost one outstanding turn per limit (the late result now publishes no second turn.completed).

desktop.followUpRelease: The release that turns limit_auto_resume on by default (LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME_ENABLED true), after the desktop runner, the Expo and the Android Limited rows ship and beta users run it for a week. That release also drops the settingRows() filter on SETTING_ROW.autoResumeAfterLimit and adds chats.autoResumeAfterLimit to FILE_SETTINGS in settings.json sync.

The Expo Limited row (OTA lane, JS only) shows only against a backend with limit_auto_resume_v1 and the flag on; the stored [[sb:limit-resume]] row shows as a notice through systemRowView.

nativeAndroid.followUpRelease: The release that turns limit_auto_resume on by default (LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME_ENABLED true), after beta users run it for a week. The Android Limited row (APK lane) shows only against a backend with limit_auto_resume_v1 and the flag on, with limitStateText as its title and limitStateDetail under it, as the desktop row does. The labs switch reaches beta users first. This change touches no package identity, signing, deep link or native module, and its migration is additive, so an older build opens a migrated database.

automated: npx vitest run tests/unit/limit-resume-rules.test.ts tests/unit/hub-db.test.ts --maxWorkers=2: limitState, shouldArm, fireChecks and nextStreak pass every case in tests/fixtures/limit-resume-cases.json; the flag helper is off by default and on with SB_LIMIT_AUTO_RESUME=1 or labs.limit_auto_resume; limit_resumes arms, fires once per request id, disarms durably, keeps the streak and keys a rotated Claude id by its root conversation.
A copy of a real 1.1 GB desktop database migrated with this build (five new tables, no other change), and the migrate code of origin/main then opened the migrated file.

npx vitest run tests/unit/limit-classification.test.ts tests/unit/acp-generic-adapter.test.ts tests/unit/codex-protocol-schema.test.ts: every case of tests/fixtures/limit-classification-cases.json passes through the real Claude adapter (SDK messages), the real Codex adapter (app-server notifications, then a failed turn/completed) and the generic ACP adapter for Gemini (a fake agent whose prompt fails with a quota error, which stays other). A full context window is context_full, not a limit; a limit followed by an empty success stays a limit; the synthetic model is never recorded and adds no tokens. The Codex fields read (error.codexErrorInfo, turn.error.codexErrorInfo) are in the app-server schema fixture.

tests/unit/limit-classification.test.ts also checks that a Claude rejection while no turn runs carries no limit, and that a late Codex limit error of a stopped turn does not mark the running turn. Full suite: npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2, 7062 passed, 4 skipped; npm run typecheck green.

npx vitest run tests/unit/limit-resumer.test.ts tests/unit/provider-registry-limit-resume.test.ts --maxWorkers=2 (fake clock, real migrated database): a chat limited with a reset in 2 minutes resumes by itself a minute after the reset; Stop before the reset means no resume, also after a restart; an armed row's timer is rebuilt at startup; 3 quick failures give up; a resumed turn that ends normally resets the streak; Resume now with the window still closed keeps the row armed; a closed window at the reset re-arms to the new reset; setting off or flag off arms nothing; no reset time asks for a manual resume; a full context window is not a limit; a normal turn end before the reset disarms; one limited turn that ends twice arms once; an open card or a chat that is not running delays the fire; another account disarms; a failed send arms again; a fire that finds a turn running tries again later; a Stop between a limit and its late second end keeps the row disarmed; a new limit starts its streak at 0. In the registry, with the limited turn and a queued message both counted as outstanding, Resume now sends the resume turn as a turn of its own (not queued) before the held queue resumes, and stores and publishes the resume row.
Full gate: npm run typecheck green; npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2, 7126 passed, 4 skipped.

Limited row polish: npx vitest run tests/unit/limit-resumer.test.ts tests/unit/settings-rows.test.ts tests/unit/settings-page-render.test.ts --maxWorkers=2 (limitStateDetail for every state; the auto-resume row stays out of search and is still bound while the flag is off). SB_VISUAL_SCOPE=screens npm run test:e2e:visual passes unchanged, so the shared Switch paints the Settings switches as before.

npm test --prefix apps/mobile -- src/components/__tests__/LimitResumeRow.test.tsx (jest, fake client): an armed row shows 'Usage limit. Resumes 3:40.' with Resume now and Cancel auto-resume; a chat that is not limited shows nothing and the row appears on limit-resume.changed (gave up, no buttons); Resume now with a closed window shows the backend's reason; Cancel calls provider:limit-resume-cancel. npx vitest run tests/unit/push-policy.test.ts tests/unit/limit-resumer.test.ts: the give-up change alone carries gaveUp and alone maps to the 'Auto-resume gave up' push.

Phone Limited rows: npx vitest run tests/unit/limit-resume-rules.test.ts --maxWorkers=2 runs the limitStateText section of tests/fixtures/limit-resume-cases.json (title and detail for every state). Expo jest src/components/__tests__/LimitResumeRow.test.tsx: the armed row shows the reset time and the detail line, a gave-up row shows its detail line. Android (./gradlew --no-daemon --max-workers=2 :app:testDebugUnitTest): LimitResumeFixturesTest runs the same section and decodes every limitState answer of the fixture; ThreadSessionCoordinatorTest checks that the row is not read without the capability, is read on open, on a limit-resume.changed that names another id and after a replay gap, and that Resume now keeps a refusal on the row and Cancel calls the backend.
notExercised: No live usage limit was hit on Claude, Codex or an ACP agent: the runner was checked with a fake adapter and a fake clock, and the classification cases are captured or constructed frames.
A chat whose session is not running at the reset (after a restart, or a closed chat) resumes only when its session starts again; restart recovery is a later change.
A message you send while the chat is idle and limited runs at once (today's behaviour) instead of joining the held queue; a message queued behind the limited turn does run after the resume turn.
No screenshot shows the restyled Limited row or the Usage limits section: both show only while the flag is on, and the screenshot run keeps it off.

The Expo and Android Limited rows were not run on a phone or against a live limit: they are checked by the jest component test, the Kotlin unit tests and the typechecks. No Robolectric screenshot shows the Android row.

Both phone apps ignore the optional row on limit-resume.changed, so the 'Usage limit reset. Resumed the chat.' notice shows on a phone only after the history reloads; the desktop appends it live. Deferred to the release that turns the flag on.
